evaluated.name: Margin Up Debt Down
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5), 0), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with improving operating margins while reducing debt intensity should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: A positive operating-margin trend indicates strengthening profitability, and falling debt-to-assets suggests the improvement is not being purchased through additional leverage. The conditional structure focuses on cases where profitability is improving and financing behavior confirms balance-sheet discipline.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Gross Profit Net Payout Bottleneck
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when strong industry-relative operating profitability coincides with net equity capital return through repurchases and dividends.
evaluated.reasoning: The bottleneck form scores firms highly only when both profitability and net payout are strong, avoiding the signed-product problem where weak-profit issuers could look attractive. Excluding gross debt issuance and repayment also reduces overlap with the broad net external financing anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Accrual Heavy Profitable Issuer
evaluated.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitable firms issuing equity should underperform when their accounting profitability is not well supported by operating cash flow.
evaluated.reasoning: High signal values require the joint presence of operating profitability, equity issuance, and accrual-heavy earnings, so unprofitable issuers are not mechanically treated as the central short case. The mechanism is not issuance alone but the combination of apparent profitability, external equity supply, and weak cash conversion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(ADD(RATIO(sstk, at), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash flow that nevertheless raise external capital through equity issuance or net debt expansion should earn lower subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids the unstable division by near-zero external financing by using a joint-rank conflict measure. The signal is high only when cash profitability and net capital raising coexist, consistent with overvaluation, aggressive expansion, or hidden funding pressure despite reported cash generation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Post Interest Net Deleverager
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, xint), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong post-interest operating surplus that are actually reducing net debt intensity should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The financing leg measures a change in debt-to-assets rather than gross debt repayment, avoiding refinancing-churn contamination. Pairing deleveraging with post-interest operating profitability emphasizes balance-sheet repair funded by operating strength rather than simple liability turnover.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Capped Net Buyback
evaluated.expression: SUB(MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), RATIO(oancf, at)), RATIO(sstk, at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most favorable when they are supported by operating cash generation and not offset by concurrent equity issuance.
evaluated.reasoning: The repurchase credit is capped by operating cash flow, so aggressive buybacks without cash support do not receive an inflated score. This avoids relying on share-count growth and instead tests whether buybacks are economically funded by current cash profitability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Peak Equity Sale
evaluated.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms issuing equity when operating profitability is near its own historical high should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Equity issuance is most suspicious when managers sell stock during peak observed profitability, when investors may overcapitalize temporarily high margins or earnings power. The historical-profitability rank prevents the signal from being merely an unprofitable-issuer proxy.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Borrowed Dividend Margin Fade
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms maintaining cash dividends while margins deteriorate and leverage rises should earn lower subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: A dividend can be a positive payout signal when supported by profits, but it becomes fragile when operating margins are weakening and debt is increasing. The nested bottleneck requires all three conditions, focusing on potentially debt-financed payout persistence rather than dividends alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Covered Dividend Compounder
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong industry-relative operating cash profitability that also make regular cash distributions should earn higher subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids the clean-surplus net-payout construction and focuses specifically on regular dividends backed by operating cash generation. The signal is high only when both cash profitability and cash distributions are strong, rather than mechanically restating broad net external financing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Reported Profit Short Debt Stress
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong reported operating profitability but weak operating cash flow and rising short-term debt intensity should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This shifts away from total liability contraction and tests a funding-stress mechanism: accounting profits look strong, but cash conversion is poor and near-term debt reliance is rising. The three-way bottleneck is intended to identify fragile profitability rather than a generic deleveraging or asset-growth effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EBITDA Current Debt Wall
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(oancf, xint), at))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with high EBITDA but weak post-interest cash generation and a large current-debt burden should earn lower subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids using changes in interest expense or total leverage, which can be mechanically collinear with debt growth. The signal instead targets firms where headline operating profitability may be misleading because cash after interest is weak and liabilities are concentrated in near-term debt.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution Resistant Profit Trend
evaluated.expression: SUB(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5), TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose operating profit per share improves faster than operating profit per asset should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This reframes share financing through the shareholder claim on operating profitability, rather than using raw share-count growth as a stand-alone anomaly. Comparing per-share and asset-scaled profit trends isolates whether financing behavior is making operating improvement accretive to each share.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Peak Profit Debt Expansion Reversal
evaluated.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(oibdp, at))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms borrowing more when profitability is near a historical peak and beginning to decelerate should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Debt expansion is most concerning when it occurs after strong profitability that may already be peaking. The added deceleration condition aims to avoid treating all profitable borrowers as shorts and instead targets firms potentially financing against a fading operating state.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Borrowed Accrual Buyback Trap
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms repurchasing shares while earnings exceed cash flow and leverage is rising should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Repurchases can be favorable when backed by cash profitability, but they are more suspect when financed alongside weak cash conversion and increasing debt intensity. The signal focuses on buyback quality rather than rediscovering net share issuance alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: External Capital Operating Productivity
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oibdp, 1), ADD(at, ADD(sstk, dltis))), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitable firms whose incremental operating profit is strong relative to their existing asset base plus newly raised capital should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the accrual-plus-financing composite with an operating productivity measure for capital already in place and capital newly issued. The denominator is anchored by assets, avoiding explosive near-zero external-financing ratios, and high values require both current profitability and productive incremental operating improvement.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Profit Net Debt Retirer
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash profitability that are net retiring long-term debt should earn higher subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Using dltr minus dltis focuses on net long-term debt retirement rather than gross repayment churn or current-debt distress. The interaction tests whether cash profitability is strong enough to reduce creditor financing, rather than simply rewarding low leverage or high cash flow in isolation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Internally Financed R&D Cash Engine
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong pre-R&D operating cash generation, meaningful R&D intensity, and low external capital issuance should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Adding back R&D avoids double-penalizing an expense already reflected in operating cash flow, while treating unreported R&D as zero is economically natural. The signal targets firms able to fund intangible investment internally rather than firms whose R&D program depends on new equity or debt issuance.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profitable Cash Maturity Spread
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms with strong reported operating profitability, those with better cash conversion and less current-debt pressure should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Prior short-term-debt stress signals produced stronger portfolio evidence than cross-sectional evidence, so this formulation creates a bipolar spread rather than a sparse short-only bottleneck. High values represent profitable firms whose earnings convert to cash without near-term refinancing strain, while low values identify profitable-looking firms exposed to cash and maturity pressure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Covered Dividend Leverage Spread
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Dividend payers whose distributions are covered by operating cash flow and not accompanied by rising leverage should outperform debt-supported dividend payers.
evaluated.reasoning: This refines the borrowed-dividend mechanism by replacing a triple condition with a continuous coverage-versus-leverage spread among dividend-paying firms. The financing leg penalizes debt expansion only when the firm is also distributing cash, focusing on payout quality rather than leverage change alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Failed Lagged Capital Raise
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital in the prior period but subsequently experience declining operating profitability should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This tests financing productivity rather than current issuance alone: capital raising is most concerning when it fails to translate into operating improvement. The lag structure helps separate the financing decision from the realized profitability outcome and gives the high-signal short leg a clear economic meaning.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: R&D Cash Payoff Net Dilution
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose pre-R&D cash generation is improving without shareholder dilution should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This shifts from static self-funding to realized R&D payoff net of dilution, so it is not the same three-way internal-financing screen. Non-R&D firms are not assigned a mechanical zero middle bucket; the R&D-intensity rank instead makes the strongest positive and negative signals come from firms where the intangible-investment mechanism is economically relevant.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Profit Payout Switch
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms increasing capital return while avoiding equity issuance should outperform cash-profitable firms that issue equity instead.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces raw share-count dilution with a financing-policy switch: payout growth versus equity issuance, conditional on industry-relative cash profitability. The signed spread gives the low tail a clear interpretation as profitable firms choosing equity issuance over cash-backed distributions, rather than a trivial product of two standalone anomalies.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Low Cost Liability Profit Quality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(xint, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with strong industry-relative operating profitability and a low interest cost burden relative to liabilities should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The profitability leg no longer subtracts interest, so interest burden is not double-counted. Scaling interest expense by total liabilities gives a cleaner financing-cost measure than adding debt to assets, and the bottleneck rewards firms where operating strength is not being eroded by costly financing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Low Cost Profit Momentum
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xint, lt), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with improving operating profitability and declining financing-cost burden should earn higher subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The signal pairs operating momentum with a financing-cost improvement rather than using leverage or issuance alone. It should favor firms whose operating gains are becoming more available to shareholders because creditors are claiming a smaller effective cost share.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self Funded Sales Margin Growth
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms growing sales while improving margins without heavy external financing should outperform externally financed growth with weak margin quality.
evaluated.reasoning: Sales growth is valuable when it scales profitably, but less so when funded through new capital while margins fail to expand. The signed spread makes the short side economically interpretable as growth financed by issuance rather than by operating improvement.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Cash Maturity Shield
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong pre-R&D cash generation and low current-debt pressure should outperform R&D firms whose intangible investment is exposed to maturity stress.
evaluated.reasoning: This combines the internally financed intangible channel with debt maturity risk rather than simply repeating an external-issuance screen. The signed spread keeps non-R&D firms closer to neutral while emphasizing R&D-heavy firms where cash generation and financing maturity are most economically relevant.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Interest Cost Shock Cash Fade
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(xint, lt), 5)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with rising financing-cost burden and deteriorating operating cash profitability should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The components reinforce a negative prediction: cash generation is weakening at the same time that liabilities are becoming more costly. This avoids putting high profitability in the short leg and focuses on a financing-cost shock interacting with fading operating strength.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issuance by cash-profitable, low-accrual firms should outperform equity issuance by firms whose reported operating profits are not cash-backed.
evaluated.reasoning: This revision abandons the blanket peak-profit issuer short story, which prior portfolio evidence contradicted, and instead diagnoses that some profitable issuers may be high-quality firms with valuable financing flexibility. Non-issuers are pushed toward neutral, while the long and short tails are separated among issuers by whether operating strength is cash-backed or accrual-heavy.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stable Cash Maturity Match
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitable firms with stable operating cash generation and low current-debt concentration should outperform profitable firms exposed to volatile cash flows and near-term refinancing pressure.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic change in debt maturity with a different mechanism: maturity risk should be most costly when cash flows are unstable. The signal keeps the successful profitability-and-financing interaction but shifts from cash-flow level versus maturity level to cash-flow stability matched against short-term debt pressure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Cash Stability Maturity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with stable pre-R&D cash generation and low current-debt pressure should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Long-horizon intangible investment is more credible when cash generation is not only high but stable, especially when near-term debt pressure is limited. This differs from the cash-level R&D maturity signal by testing cash-flow durability as the profitability leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Productive Equity Issuer Quality
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issuers with improving real operating profitability and low accrual dependence should outperform accrual-heavy issuers without operating improvement.
evaluated.reasoning: Prior evidence suggested that not all profitable issuers should be treated as shorts, so this ranks issuance quality rather than issuance itself. The signal separates firms issuing into genuine operating improvement from firms issuing while reported profits are not cash-backed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Productive Debt Issuer Margin
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt issuance should be more favorable when accompanied by margin improvement and low financing costs.
evaluated.reasoning: This treats debt issuance as potentially productive rather than mechanically bad, with the payoff depending on whether operating margins are improving enough to justify the financing. High-cost liability structures penalize debt issuers whose new borrowing may be more burdensome than productive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Growth Cash Maturity Match
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Sales growth should be more valuable when it is supported by cash margins and not exposed to near-term debt refinancing pressure.
evaluated.reasoning: Growth funded or accompanied by weak cash profitability can destroy value, especially when short-term liabilities constrain reinvestment. The interaction emphasizes growth firms whose operating cash economics and financing maturity are aligned.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: R&D Harvest Payout Trap
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms returning capital while cutting R&D intensity without corresponding operating-margin improvement should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This shifts away from the already-tested R&D cash-plus-financing-cost channel and instead tests whether payouts are being supported by underinvestment rather than durable operating strength. The signed spread gives the low tail a coherent opposite case: payout firms with improving margins and no R&D harvest.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Durable Cash Payout Cost Shield
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Capital-return firms with stable operating cash generation and low liability funding costs should outperform payout firms exposed to volatile cash flows and expensive financing.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids mechanically subtracting payouts from the profitability leg, so payout size no longer directly creates worse “coverage.” The interaction instead asks whether distributions are supported by durable cash economics and benign financing costs, separating high-quality capital return from strained payout behavior.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Rollover Profit Cost Reset
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms actively rolling over debt should outperform when refinancing coincides with improving operating profitability and falling liability funding cost.
evaluated.reasoning: Gross debt repayment alone can reflect churn, so this uses the overlap of issuance and repayment to identify actual refinancing episodes. The signal separates productive refinancing from stressed rollover by comparing operating-profit improvement against changes in the cost of liabilities.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Current Debt R&D Retrenchment
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D firms with high current-debt pressure that are cutting R&D intensity without strong pre-R&D cash generation should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids recombining the prior R&D cash-maturity and growth-maturity winners, and instead tests whether short-term financing pressure forces intangible underinvestment. The high-signal short leg is not simply R&D-heavy growth; it is a maturity-pressure case where apparent cash constraints coincide with R&D retrenchment.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilutive Buyback Cash Gap
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms reporting large repurchases while share count still rises and operating cash profitability is weak should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves away from the debt-issuer margin spread and focuses on buyback effectiveness: gross repurchase dollars are suspect when they fail to reduce dilution. Pairing the dilution outcome with operating cash profitability distinguishes cash-backed shareholder return from repurchases that merely offset equity compensation or financing needs.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Current Debt Gross Margin Squeeze
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration and worsening gross cost intensity relative to sales growth should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids the redundant low-operating-cash-flow construction criticized in the prior current-debt trap. The mechanism is operating pressure at the gross-margin level interacting with refinancing risk: near-term liabilities are more dangerous when unit economics deteriorate and sales growth does not compensate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Levered Cash Carry Advantage
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Liability-intensive firms should outperform when operating cash generation per dollar of liabilities exceeds the interest cost burden.
evaluated.reasoning: The liability-intensity gate makes the signal about productive use of financing rather than a trivial profitability-minus-interest spread across all firms. High values identify firms where liabilities appear to fund cash-generating operations at a favorable carry, while low values capture leveraged firms whose cash output does not cover financing cost well.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Externally Funded SG&A Productivity Gap
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(xsga, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(revt, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms raising external capital while SG&A grows faster than revenue should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This preserves the overhead-efficiency idea without mechanically double-counting operating-margin deterioration through oibdp. The signal targets externally financed organizational expansion that is not yet producing revenue growth, a distinct failure mode from generic external financing or margin decline alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Lagged Capital Profit Payoff
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital in the prior period should outperform when operating profitability improves faster than the asset base expands.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the weak lagged-capital-raise short idea by asking whether financing produced operating payoff, not merely whether profitability declined. High values identify prior capital raisers with improving profit productivity, while low values capture asset expansion without corresponding operating gains.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Costly Debt Paydown Cash Relief
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-generative firms retiring high-cost debt should outperform firms continuing to issue or roll into costly debt.
evaluated.reasoning: Net long-term debt retirement alone had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak alpha, so this conditions paydown on the economic benefit of retiring expensive liabilities. The signal is highest when cash flow can fund relief from high interest burden and lowest when costly debt exposure is being increased.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Externally Funded R&D Commercialization Gap
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms raising external capital while R&D intensity rises faster than revenue productivity should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the current-debt/R&D-retrenchment setup with a commercialization-failure mechanism: external capital is funding intangible buildout, but sales productivity is not following. The short leg is not simply maturity pressure or weak cash flow; it is financed R&D expansion without evidence of revenue conversion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Equity Issuer Interest Relief Margin Hold
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issuers should outperform when issuance reduces financing-cost pressure while operating margins are preserved or improving.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves away from cash-backed issuer and debt-maturity repair components and instead tests equity issuance as a balance-sheet cost-reset mechanism. High values identify issuers whose financing burden falls without operating deterioration, while low values capture issuers with rising cost pressure and weakening margins.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Flow Dividend Commitment Spread
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Dividend increases backed by improving operating cash flow and little equity issuance should outperform dividend increases coinciding with weak cash flow and dilution.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a gross-margin/maturity substitution; it tests whether a rising cash dividend is a credible commitment signal or a financing-strained payout. The financing interaction comes from distinguishing cash-flow-backed dividend growth from dividend growth accompanied by equity issuance.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Proceeds Payout Diversion
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that recently issued long-term debt and subsequently emphasize payouts over operating-profit improvement should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the debt-issuer cash-carry delta construction with a use-of-proceeds mechanism. High values indicate lagged borrowing followed by capital return without operating payoff, whereas low values identify debt issuers whose subsequent profitability improvement dominates payout use.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Equity Deleveraging Cash Issuer
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issuers should outperform when proceeds appear to support debt reduction and the firm is not issuing to cover weak operating cash flow.
evaluated.reasoning: This treats equity issuance as potentially constructive when it repairs the balance sheet rather than as uniformly negative dilution. The low tail is economically interpretable as equity issuers with poor cash generation and net debt expansion, while the high tail captures cash-generative deleveraging issuers.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Current Debt R&D Cost Shock
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), MIN(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration that cut R&D intensity while liability funding costs rise should underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The mechanism is refinancing pressure forcing intangible underinvestment, not merely weak cash flow or low R&D. Rising interest burden makes current-debt pressure more binding, and a simultaneous R&D cut suggests the financing shock is impairing long-run operating capacity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: External Capital Operating Leverage Payoff
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(oibdp, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(xsga, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that recently raised external capital should outperform when operating profit grows faster than overhead.
evaluated.reasoning: This tests whether external financing translates into operating leverage rather than organizational bloat. High values indicate prior capital raises followed by profit scaling faster than SG&A, while low values identify externally funded overhead growth without commensurate operating payoff.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Financed Asset Renewal Quality
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt issuers with strong operating cash generation relative to depreciation burden should outperform debt issuers whose asset base appears costly to maintain.
evaluated.reasoning: Debt issuance can be productive when it supports assets that generate cash flow, but risky when cash generation is weak relative to the depreciation burden. The interaction evaluates debt-financed asset renewal quality rather than debt issuance alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: R&D Payoff Shareholder Accretion
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms should outperform when intangible investment translates into rising operating profit per share without dilution.
evaluated.reasoning: This leaves the cash-maturity channel and instead tests whether R&D spending is becoming accretive to existing shareholders. The financing leg is share dilution, but it is evaluated only in the context of per-share operating-profit payoff from intangible investment rather than as a standalone net-share-issuance anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rollover Cash Coverage Strain
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(xint, lt)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, xint))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms actively refinancing debt should underperform when interest burden is high and operating cash flow poorly covers interest expense.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the rollover question from marginal cost or maturity improvement to coverage strain during refinancing episodes. High values identify firms rolling debt while creditors are already expensive and cash coverage is weak, a stressed refinancing mechanism rather than a marginal variant of prior rollover-profit payoff tests.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Lagged Capital Gross Profit Payoff
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital should outperform when subsequent gross-profit productivity improves faster than the asset base expands.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the growth indicator with a lagged financing-payoff test, avoiding the middle-bucket problem for non-growers. The signal asks whether external capital translated into better gross operating economics rather than mere balance-sheet expansion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Lagged Financed R&D Commercialization
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(revt, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that recently raised capital should outperform when revenue productivity improves more than R&D intensity rises.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves away from the static R&D cash-maturity runway and tests commercialization after external financing. High values require prior capital raising, meaningful R&D intensity, and evidence that the intangible program is converting into revenue productivity rather than simply consuming more capital.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Current Debt Dividend Cash Squeeze
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration should underperform when dividend commitments rise faster than operating cash flow.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the generic current-debt-plus-fundamental-deterioration setup with a payout-crowding mechanism. Near-term refinancing risk is more problematic when cash distributions are increasing while operating cash generation is not keeping pace.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rollover Maintenance Cash Strain
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(dp, at)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms actively rolling over debt should underperform when depreciation burden is high and operating cash profitability is weak.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the rollover mechanism from R&D cost shock to asset-maintenance strain. High values identify refinancers whose cash generation may be insufficient relative to the depreciation burden of the asset base, suggesting rollover risk is tied to weak operating asset quality.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Lagged Debt Gross Profit Efficiency
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(SUB(revt, cogs), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(lt, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that issued long-term debt should outperform when subsequent gross profit grows faster than liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: This fixes the contemporaneous timing issue by lagging debt issuance and avoids simply negating the SG&A-productivity spread. The signal tests whether borrowed capital produces scalable gross-profit growth rather than merely increasing liability claims.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Buyback Cash Acceleration Discipline
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(oancf, at))), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Repurchasing firms should outperform when buybacks coincide with accelerating operating cash profitability and little new debt issuance.
evaluated.reasoning: This avoids the prior dilution-leg scaling problem by dropping the mixed raw share-count and issuance sum. The mechanism is buyback timing and funding quality: repurchases are more credible when cash generation is accelerating and less credible when paired with debt issuance.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin Up Debt Down
considered.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5), 0), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with improving operating margins while reducing debt intensity should outperform.
considered.reasoning: A positive operating-margin trend indicates strengthening profitability, and falling debt-to-assets suggests the improvement is not being purchased through additional leverage. The conditional structure focuses on cases where profitability is improving and financing behavior confirms balance-sheet discipline.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Gross Profit Net Payout Bottleneck
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when strong industry-relative operating profitability coincides with net equity capital return through repurchases and dividends.
considered.reasoning: The bottleneck form scores firms highly only when both profitability and net payout are strong, avoiding the signed-product problem where weak-profit issuers could look attractive. Excluding gross debt issuance and repayment also reduces overlap with the broad net external financing anomaly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual Heavy Profitable Issuer
considered.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Profitable firms issuing equity should underperform when their accounting profitability is not well supported by operating cash flow.
considered.reasoning: High signal values require the joint presence of operating profitability, equity issuance, and accrual-heavy earnings, so unprofitable issuers are not mechanically treated as the central short case. The mechanism is not issuance alone but the combination of apparent profitability, external equity supply, and weak cash conversion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(ADD(RATIO(sstk, at), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash flow that nevertheless raise external capital through equity issuance or net debt expansion should earn lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the unstable division by near-zero external financing by using a joint-rank conflict measure. The signal is high only when cash profitability and net capital raising coexist, consistent with overvaluation, aggressive expansion, or hidden funding pressure despite reported cash generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Post Interest Net Deleverager
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, xint), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong post-interest operating surplus that are actually reducing net debt intensity should outperform.
considered.reasoning: The financing leg measures a change in debt-to-assets rather than gross debt repayment, avoiding refinancing-churn contamination. Pairing deleveraging with post-interest operating profitability emphasizes balance-sheet repair funded by operating strength rather than simple liability turnover.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Capped Net Buyback
considered.expression: SUB(MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), RATIO(oancf, at)), RATIO(sstk, at))
considered.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most favorable when they are supported by operating cash generation and not offset by concurrent equity issuance.
considered.reasoning: The repurchase credit is capped by operating cash flow, so aggressive buybacks without cash support do not receive an inflated score. This avoids relying on share-count growth and instead tests whether buybacks are economically funded by current cash profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Peak Equity Sale
considered.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms issuing equity when operating profitability is near its own historical high should underperform.
considered.reasoning: Equity issuance is most suspicious when managers sell stock during peak observed profitability, when investors may overcapitalize temporarily high margins or earnings power. The historical-profitability rank prevents the signal from being merely an unprofitable-issuer proxy.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Borrowed Dividend Margin Fade
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms maintaining cash dividends while margins deteriorate and leverage rises should earn lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: A dividend can be a positive payout signal when supported by profits, but it becomes fragile when operating margins are weakening and debt is increasing. The nested bottleneck requires all three conditions, focusing on potentially debt-financed payout persistence rather than dividends alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Covered Dividend Compounder
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong industry-relative operating cash profitability that also make regular cash distributions should earn higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the clean-surplus net-payout construction and focuses specifically on regular dividends backed by operating cash generation. The signal is high only when both cash profitability and cash distributions are strong, rather than mechanically restating broad net external financing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Reported Profit Short Debt Stress
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong reported operating profitability but weak operating cash flow and rising short-term debt intensity should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This shifts away from total liability contraction and tests a funding-stress mechanism: accounting profits look strong, but cash conversion is poor and near-term debt reliance is rising. The three-way bottleneck is intended to identify fragile profitability rather than a generic deleveraging or asset-growth effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EBITDA Current Debt Wall
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(oancf, xint), at))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with high EBITDA but weak post-interest cash generation and a large current-debt burden should earn lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This avoids using changes in interest expense or total leverage, which can be mechanically collinear with debt growth. The signal instead targets firms where headline operating profitability may be misleading because cash after interest is weak and liabilities are concentrated in near-term debt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dilution Resistant Profit Trend
considered.expression: SUB(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5), TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose operating profit per share improves faster than operating profit per asset should outperform.
considered.reasoning: This reframes share financing through the shareholder claim on operating profitability, rather than using raw share-count growth as a stand-alone anomaly. Comparing per-share and asset-scaled profit trends isolates whether financing behavior is making operating improvement accretive to each share.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Peak Profit Debt Expansion Reversal
considered.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(oibdp, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms borrowing more when profitability is near a historical peak and beginning to decelerate should underperform.
considered.reasoning: Debt expansion is most concerning when it occurs after strong profitability that may already be peaking. The added deceleration condition aims to avoid treating all profitable borrowers as shorts and instead targets firms potentially financing against a fading operating state.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Borrowed Accrual Buyback Trap
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms repurchasing shares while earnings exceed cash flow and leverage is rising should underperform.
considered.reasoning: Repurchases can be favorable when backed by cash profitability, but they are more suspect when financed alongside weak cash conversion and increasing debt intensity. The signal focuses on buyback quality rather than rediscovering net share issuance alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: External Capital Operating Productivity
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oibdp, 1), ADD(at, ADD(sstk, dltis))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Profitable firms whose incremental operating profit is strong relative to their existing asset base plus newly raised capital should outperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the accrual-plus-financing composite with an operating productivity measure for capital already in place and capital newly issued. The denominator is anchored by assets, avoiding explosive near-zero external-financing ratios, and high values require both current profitability and productive incremental operating improvement.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profit Net Debt Retirer
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash profitability that are net retiring long-term debt should earn higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Using dltr minus dltis focuses on net long-term debt retirement rather than gross repayment churn or current-debt distress. The interaction tests whether cash profitability is strong enough to reduce creditor financing, rather than simply rewarding low leverage or high cash flow in isolation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Equity Claim Cash Accretion
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, ceq), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose cash generation improves for the common equity claim faster than for the overall asset base should outperform.
considered.reasoning: This fixes the unit mismatch by comparing ranked trends in two unitless cash-return ratios rather than subtracting dollars-per-share from an asset ratio. It also avoids raw share-count growth and instead asks whether financing structure is making operating cash generation more accretive to book equity holders.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Internally Financed R&D Cash Engine
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong pre-R&D operating cash generation, meaningful R&D intensity, and low external capital issuance should outperform.
considered.reasoning: Adding back R&D avoids double-penalizing an expense already reflected in operating cash flow, while treating unreported R&D as zero is economically natural. The signal targets firms able to fund intangible investment internally rather than firms whose R&D program depends on new equity or debt issuance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profitable Cash Maturity Spread
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with strong reported operating profitability, those with better cash conversion and less current-debt pressure should outperform.
considered.reasoning: Prior short-term-debt stress signals produced stronger portfolio evidence than cross-sectional evidence, so this formulation creates a bipolar spread rather than a sparse short-only bottleneck. High values represent profitable firms whose earnings convert to cash without near-term refinancing strain, while low values identify profitable-looking firms exposed to cash and maturity pressure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Covered Dividend Leverage Spread
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Dividend payers whose distributions are covered by operating cash flow and not accompanied by rising leverage should outperform debt-supported dividend payers.
considered.reasoning: This refines the borrowed-dividend mechanism by replacing a triple condition with a continuous coverage-versus-leverage spread among dividend-paying firms. The financing leg penalizes debt expansion only when the firm is also distributing cash, focusing on payout quality rather than leverage change alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Failed Lagged Capital Raise
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital in the prior period but subsequently experience declining operating profitability should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This tests financing productivity rather than current issuance alone: capital raising is most concerning when it fails to translate into operating improvement. The lag structure helps separate the financing decision from the realized profitability outcome and gives the high-signal short leg a clear economic meaning.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Cash Payoff Net Dilution
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose pre-R&D cash generation is improving without shareholder dilution should outperform.
considered.reasoning: This shifts from static self-funding to realized R&D payoff net of dilution, so it is not the same three-way internal-financing screen. Non-R&D firms are not assigned a mechanical zero middle bucket; the R&D-intensity rank instead makes the strongest positive and negative signals come from firms where the intangible-investment mechanism is economically relevant.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profit Payout Switch
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms increasing capital return while avoiding equity issuance should outperform cash-profitable firms that issue equity instead.
considered.reasoning: This replaces raw share-count dilution with a financing-policy switch: payout growth versus equity issuance, conditional on industry-relative cash profitability. The signed spread gives the low tail a clear interpretation as profitable firms choosing equity issuance over cash-backed distributions, rather than a trivial product of two standalone anomalies.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Low Cost Liability Profit Quality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(xint, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with strong industry-relative operating profitability and a low interest cost burden relative to liabilities should outperform.
considered.reasoning: The profitability leg no longer subtracts interest, so interest burden is not double-counted. Scaling interest expense by total liabilities gives a cleaner financing-cost measure than adding debt to assets, and the bottleneck rewards firms where operating strength is not being eroded by costly financing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Low Cost Profit Momentum
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xint, lt), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with improving operating profitability and declining financing-cost burden should earn higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The signal pairs operating momentum with a financing-cost improvement rather than using leverage or issuance alone. It should favor firms whose operating gains are becoming more available to shareholders because creditors are claiming a smaller effective cost share.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Sales Margin Growth
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms growing sales while improving margins without heavy external financing should outperform externally financed growth with weak margin quality.
considered.reasoning: Sales growth is valuable when it scales profitably, but less so when funded through new capital while margins fail to expand. The signed spread makes the short side economically interpretable as growth financed by issuance rather than by operating improvement.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Cash Maturity Shield
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong pre-R&D cash generation and low current-debt pressure should outperform R&D firms whose intangible investment is exposed to maturity stress.
considered.reasoning: This combines the internally financed intangible channel with debt maturity risk rather than simply repeating an external-issuance screen. The signed spread keeps non-R&D firms closer to neutral while emphasizing R&D-heavy firms where cash generation and financing maturity are most economically relevant.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Interest Cost Shock Cash Fade
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(xint, lt), 5)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with rising financing-cost burden and deteriorating operating cash profitability should underperform.
considered.reasoning: The components reinforce a negative prediction: cash generation is weakening at the same time that liabilities are becoming more costly. This avoids putting high profitability in the short leg and focuses on a financing-cost shock interacting with fading operating strength.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuance by cash-profitable, low-accrual firms should outperform equity issuance by firms whose reported operating profits are not cash-backed.
considered.reasoning: This revision abandons the blanket peak-profit issuer short story, which prior portfolio evidence contradicted, and instead diagnoses that some profitable issuers may be high-quality firms with valuable financing flexibility. Non-issuers are pushed toward neutral, while the long and short tails are separated among issuers by whether operating strength is cash-backed or accrual-heavy.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stable Cash Maturity Match
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitable firms with stable operating cash generation and low current-debt concentration should outperform profitable firms exposed to volatile cash flows and near-term refinancing pressure.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic change in debt maturity with a different mechanism: maturity risk should be most costly when cash flows are unstable. The signal keeps the successful profitability-and-financing interaction but shifts from cash-flow level versus maturity level to cash-flow stability matched against short-term debt pressure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Cash Stability Maturity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with stable pre-R&D cash generation and low current-debt pressure should outperform.
considered.reasoning: Long-horizon intangible investment is more credible when cash generation is not only high but stable, especially when near-term debt pressure is limited. This differs from the cash-level R&D maturity signal by testing cash-flow durability as the profitability leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Productive Equity Issuer Quality
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuers with improving real operating profitability and low accrual dependence should outperform accrual-heavy issuers without operating improvement.
considered.reasoning: Prior evidence suggested that not all profitable issuers should be treated as shorts, so this ranks issuance quality rather than issuance itself. The signal separates firms issuing into genuine operating improvement from firms issuing while reported profits are not cash-backed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Productive Debt Issuer Margin
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt issuance should be more favorable when accompanied by margin improvement and low financing costs.
considered.reasoning: This treats debt issuance as potentially productive rather than mechanically bad, with the payoff depending on whether operating margins are improving enough to justify the financing. High-cost liability structures penalize debt issuers whose new borrowing may be more burdensome than productive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Growth Cash Maturity Match
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Sales growth should be more valuable when it is supported by cash margins and not exposed to near-term debt refinancing pressure.
considered.reasoning: Growth funded or accompanied by weak cash profitability can destroy value, especially when short-term liabilities constrain reinvestment. The interaction emphasizes growth firms whose operating cash economics and financing maturity are aligned.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Harvest Payout Trap
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1))))

considered.reasoning: This shifts away from the already-tested R&D cash-plus-financing-cost channel and instead tests whether payouts are being supported by underinvestment rather than durable operating strength. The signed spread gives the low tail a coherent opposite case: payout firms with improving margins and no R&D harvest.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Durable Cash Payout Cost Shield
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1), SUB(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Capital-return firms with stable operating cash generation and low liability funding costs should outperform payout firms exposed to volatile cash flows and expensive financing.
considered.reasoning: This avoids mechanically subtracting payouts from the profitability leg, so payout size no longer directly creates worse “coverage.” The interaction instead asks whether distributions are supported by durable cash economics and benign financing costs, separating high-quality capital return from strained payout behavior.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Rollover Profit Cost Reset
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms actively rolling over debt should outperform when refinancing coincides with improving operating profitability and falling liability funding cost.
considered.reasoning: Gross debt repayment alone can reflect churn, so this uses the overlap of issuance and repayment to identify actual refinancing episodes. The signal separates productive refinancing from stressed rollover by comparing operating-profit improvement against changes in the cost of liabilities.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current Debt R&D Retrenchment
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))))

considered.name: Dilutive Buyback Cash Gap
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms reporting large repurchases while share count still rises and operating cash profitability is weak should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This moves away from the debt-issuer margin spread and focuses on buyback effectiveness: gross repurchase dollars are suspect when they fail to reduce dilution. Pairing the dilution outcome with operating cash profitability distinguishes cash-backed shareholder return from repurchases that merely offset equity compensation or financing needs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current Debt Gross Margin Squeeze
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration and worsening gross cost intensity relative to sales growth should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the redundant low-operating-cash-flow construction criticized in the prior current-debt trap. considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Levered Cash Carry Advantage
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Liability-intensive firms should outperform when operating cash generation per dollar of liabilities exceeds the interest cost burden.
considered.reasoning: The liability-intensity gate makes the signal about productive use of financing rather than a trivial profitability-minus-interest spread across all firms. High values identify firms where liabilities appear to fund cash-generating operations at a favorable carry, while low values capture leveraged firms whose cash output does not cover financing cost well.

considered.name: Externally Funded SG&A Productivity Gap
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(xsga, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(revt, 1))))

considered.reasoning: This preserves the overhead-efficiency idea without mechanically double-counting operating-margin deterioration through oibdp. The signal targets externally financed organizational expansion that is not yet producing revenue growth, a distinct failure mode from generic external financing or margin decline alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Lagged Capital Profit Payoff
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital in the prior period should outperform when operating profitability improves faster than the asset base expands.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the weak lagged-capital-raise short idea by asking whether financing produced operating payoff, not merely whether profitability declined. High values identify prior capital raisers with improving profit productivity, while low values capture asset expansion without corresponding operating gains.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Costly Debt Paydown Cash Relief
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))

considered.reasoning: Net long-term debt retirement alone had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak alpha, so this conditions paydown on the economic benefit of retiring expensive liabilities. The signal is highest when cash flow can fund relief from high interest burden and lowest when costly debt exposure is being increased.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Externally Funded R&D Commercialization Gap
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 5))))
