considered.reasoning: This replaces the current-debt/R&D-retrenchment setup with a commercialization-failure mechanism: external capital is funding intangible buildout, but sales productivity is not following. The short leg is not simply maturity pressure or weak cash flow; it is financed R&D expansion without evidence of revenue conversion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Equity Issuer Interest Relief Margin Hold
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuers should outperform when issuance reduces financing-cost pressure while operating margins are preserved or improving.
considered.reasoning: This moves away from cash-backed issuer and debt-maturity repair components and instead tests equity issuance as a balance-sheet cost-reset mechanism. High values identify issuers whose financing burden falls without operating deterioration, while low values capture issuers with rising cost pressure and weakening margins.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Flow Dividend Commitment Spread
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Dividend increases backed by improving operating cash flow and little equity issuance should outperform dividend increases coinciding with weak cash flow and dilution.
considered.reasoning: This is not a gross-margin/maturity substitution; it tests whether a rising cash dividend is a credible commitment signal or a financing-strained payout. The financing interaction comes from distinguishing cash-flow-backed dividend growth from dividend growth accompanied by equity issuance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Proceeds Payout Diversion
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that recently issued long-term debt and subsequently emphasize payouts over operating-profit improvement should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the debt-issuer cash-carry delta construction with a use-of-proceeds mechanism. High values indicate lagged borrowing followed by capital return without operating payoff, whereas low values identify debt issuers whose subsequent profitability improvement dominates payout use.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Equity Deleveraging Cash Issuer
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuers should outperform when proceeds appear to support debt reduction and the firm is not issuing to cover weak operating cash flow.
considered.reasoning: This treats equity issuance as potentially constructive when it repairs the balance sheet rather than as uniformly negative dilution. The low tail is economically interpretable as equity issuers with poor cash generation and net debt expansion, while the high tail captures cash-generative deleveraging issuers.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current Debt R&D Cost Shock
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), MIN(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xint, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration that cut R&D intensity while liability funding costs rise should underperform.
considered.reasoning: The mechanism is refinancing pressure forcing intangible underinvestment, not merely weak cash flow or low R&D. Rising interest burden makes current-debt pressure more binding, and a simultaneous R&D cut suggests the financing shock is impairing long-run operating capacity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: External Capital Operating Leverage Payoff
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(oibdp, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(xsga, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that recently raised external capital should outperform when operating profit grows faster than overhead.
considered.reasoning: This tests whether external financing translates into operating leverage rather than organizational bloat. High values indicate prior capital raises followed by profit scaling faster than SG&A, while low values identify externally funded overhead growth without commensurate operating payoff.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Financed Asset Renewal Quality
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt issuers with strong operating cash generation relative to depreciation burden should outperform debt issuers whose asset base appears costly to maintain.
considered.reasoning: Debt issuance can be productive when it supports assets that generate cash flow, but risky when cash generation is weak relative to the depreciation burden. The interaction evaluates debt-financed asset renewal quality rather than debt issuance alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Payoff Shareholder Accretion
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms should outperform when intangible investment translates into rising operating profit per share without dilution.
considered.reasoning: This leaves the cash-maturity channel and instead tests whether R&D spending is becoming accretive to existing shareholders. The financing leg is share dilution, but it is evaluated only in the context of per-share operating-profit payoff from intangible investment rather than as a standalone net-share-issuance anomaly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rollover Cash Coverage Strain
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(xint, lt)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, xint))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms actively refinancing debt should underperform when interest burden is high and operating cash flow poorly covers interest expense.
considered.reasoning: This changes the rollover question from marginal cost or maturity improvement to coverage strain during refinancing episodes. High values identify firms rolling debt while creditors are already expensive and cash coverage is weak, a stressed refinancing mechanism rather than a marginal variant of prior rollover-profit payoff tests.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Lagged Capital Gross Profit Payoff
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital should outperform when subsequent gross-profit productivity improves faster than the asset base expands.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the growth indicator with a lagged financing-payoff test, avoiding the middle-bucket problem for non-growers. The signal asks whether external capital translated into better gross operating economics rather than mere balance-sheet expansion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Lagged Financed R&D Commercialization
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(revt, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that recently raised capital should outperform when revenue productivity improves more than R&D intensity rises.
considered.reasoning: This moves away from the static R&D cash-maturity runway and tests commercialization after external financing. High values require prior capital raising, meaningful R&D intensity, and evidence that the intangible program is converting into revenue productivity rather than simply consuming more capital.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current Debt Dividend Cash Squeeze
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with high current-debt concentration should underperform when dividend commitments rise faster than operating cash flow.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the generic current-debt-plus-fundamental-deterioration setup with a payout-crowding mechanism. Near-term refinancing risk is more problematic when cash distributions are increasing while operating cash generation is not keeping pace.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rollover Maintenance Cash Strain
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(dltis, dltr), at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(dp, at)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms actively rolling over debt should underperform when depreciation burden is high and operating cash profitability is weak.
considered.reasoning: This changes the rollover mechanism from R&D cost shock to asset-maintenance strain. High values identify refinancers whose cash generation may be insufficient relative to the depreciation burden of the asset base, suggesting rollover risk is tied to weak operating asset quality.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Lagged Debt Gross Profit Efficiency
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(dltis, at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(SUB(revt, cogs), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(lt, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that issued long-term debt should outperform when subsequent gross profit grows faster than liabilities.
considered.reasoning: This fixes the contemporaneous timing issue by lagging debt issuance and avoids simply negating the SG&A-productivity spread. The signal tests whether borrowed capital produces scalable gross-profit growth rather than merely increasing liability claims.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Buyback Cash Acceleration Discipline
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(oancf, at))), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Repurchasing firms should outperform when buybacks coincide with accelerating operating cash profitability and little new debt issuance.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the prior dilution-leg scaling problem by dropping the mixed raw share-count and issuance sum. The mechanism is buyback timing and funding quality: repurchases are more credible when cash generation is accelerating and less credible when paired with debt issuance.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the well-documented net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) multiplied by gross profitability, and the multiplicative form is internally inconsistent because a below-industry-profitability firm that is net *issuing* capital produces a large positive product (predicted high return), the exact opposite of the stated hypothesis.

With a signed industry-adjusted profitability term and a strictly non-negative issuance term, the most negative signal values belong to *unprofitable* issuers, so the expected-negative sign implies those firms earn the highest returns — contradicting both the hypothesis and the known equity-issuance evidence, on top of largely rediscovering the issuance anomaly itself.

The ratio's denominator (sstk+dltis) is zero or near-zero for a large fraction of firms, making the statistic explosive and sign-unstable (negative oancf over tiny issuance flips ordering), so 1% winsorization cannot rescue it and the surviving variation is little more than an inverse external-financing proxy.

The rank-product construction is at least sign-safe, but dltr is *gross* long-term debt repayment — high values often reflect refinancing churn rather than deleveraging — so the expression does not measure the hypothesized balance-sheet improvement, and the profitability-plus-payout mechanism duplicates three sibling proposals in this batch.

The conditional gating on a multi-period margin trend applied to the change in leverage is coherent, sign-consistent, and the most economically distinct proposal here, though it leans on the known debt-issuance/leverage-change anomaly and lumps all declining-margin firms at exactly zero, which will blunt the cross-sectional slope.

Share-count growth is the canonical net-share-issuance anomaly (Pontiff-Woodgate, Daniel-Titman) and will dominate the product since the profitability rank is a bounded positive scalar, so this is a rediscovery with a mild profitability tilt rather than a new interaction.

Because clean-surplus accounting makes (ni − Δceq) essentially net payout (dividends + repurchases − issuance, contaminated by OCI), this is a near-mechanical restatement of the archive's already-tested "Gross Profit Net Payout Bottleneck" (profitability IND_RANK ∧ net-payout RANK) and also overlaps the published net-payout/composite-issuance anomalies.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's "Post Interest Net Deleverager" and the inverse of "Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict" — cash profitability bottlenecked with falling liability intensity — with Δ(lt/at) highly collinear with Δ(debt/at) and largely subsumed by the known asset-growth/NOA-change anomalies.

Conditioning equity issuance on the firm's own time-series profitability peak is a defensible market-timing refinement that is internally consistent with the negative sign and distinct from the archive's accrual-based issuer conditioning, though it remains a variant of the well-documented share-issuance anomaly with sstk-driven low coverage and a noisy long leg under the MIN construction.

The debt-financed-dividend-with-fading-margins story is economically coherent and sign-consistent, but the triple nested MIN plus a 5-period trend and dvc requirement will compress cross-sectional variation and coverage, so the main risk is a statistically fragile, composition-unstable spread rather than a conceptual flaw.

This is essentially the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's "Post Interest Net Deleverager" with Δ(xint/at) mechanically collinear with Δ(debt/at), and the MIN puts a known positive predictor (high profitability) inside the short leg, so the two components fight each other rather than reinforcing the hypothesis.

Self-admittedly a refinement of the failed gen-0 "Margin Up Debt Down" (indicator replaced by rank, plus an issuance leg already explored in "Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict"), which makes it a cosmetic rather than substantive change to a mechanism the archive has already found weak.

This is essentially the Sloan accruals anomaly intersected with the net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), i.e., a documented composite rather than a new mechanism, and it is a near-relative of the archived "Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict"/"Accrual Heavy Profitable Issuer" pair with the same MIN structure that leaves the long leg (low value) economically undefined.

It is largely the sign-flipped, one-leg-lighter version of the already-evaluated "EBITDA Current Debt Wall" (same post-interest cash and dlc/lt ingredients), so it recycles archived content while reducing to a generic cash-profitability-plus-low-short-term-debt (distress) composite.

A cosmetic fundamental swap (oancf for oibdp) on the archived "Dilution Resistant Profit Trend," and the construction is unit-inconsistent — a dollars-per-share trend minus a unitless ratio trend is numerically dominated by the first term, so the signal is really just cash-flow-per-share growth (share-count/dilution) rather than the stated relative comparison.

The three conditions (own-history profitability peak, rising debt intensity, decelerating profitability) are internally consistent with the negative expected sign and the mechanism is economically sensible, though the triple-MIN conjunction risks the same diluted-long-leg / near-zero Fama-MacBeth slope pathology seen in the archived three-way MIN signals.

Internally inconsistent: R&D is already expensed within operating cash flow, so subtracting xrd again double-penalizes R&D intensity and the leg measures the opposite of "cash sufficient to cover R&D," and requiring non-missing xrd will further shrink already-thin coverage.

The debt-financed, accrual-backed repurchase conjunction is a coherent buyback-quality story with sign and expression aligned, but it overlaps the known leveraged-repurchase and accruals literatures and the three-way MIN will likely produce a very sparse, unstable short leg.

This is largely a re-parameterization of the archive's "Internally Financed R&D Cash Engine" (same three ingredients, same mechanism), and the INDICATOR multiplication is technically broken because non-R&D firms are assigned exactly 0, which places them in the *middle* of a signed spread that ranges negative-to-positive, contaminating both tails with a mechanically distinct subpopulation.

The bipolar reformulation is a defensible response to the diagnosed fmb/alpha divergence in the earlier short-term-debt bottleneck signals and the sign logic is internally consistent, though the multiplicative weighting by a strictly positive IND_RANK compresses low-profitability firms toward neutral and the components (profitability, cash conversion, debt maturity) are each individually well-documented.

Payout coverage net of concurrent leverage expansion is a coherent and correctly signed refinement of the weak "Borrowed Dividend Margin Fade" idea, but the RANK(dvc/at) gate assigns non-payers a large tied mid-low rank rather than zero, so the intended "among dividend payers" conditioning is only partial and the leverage-change leg is close to the known debt-issuance anomaly.

This is a plain multiplicative pairing of two well-published anomalies (profitability trend and composite/share issuance) and covers essentially the same economic ground as the archive's "Dilution Resistant Profit Trend," so it is both a near-rediscovery and too trivial in construction to be informative.

The expression, sign, and lag alignment are internally consistent and the ex-post "financing failed to produce profit growth" conditioning is a genuine step beyond the archive's contemporaneous issuance signals, though it sits close to the established external-financing anomaly and the MIN bottleneck will again make the informative leg sparse.

The two legs both subtract/scale by xint so the spread double-counts interest burden rather than combining distinct information, and the denominator ADD(at, dltt, dlc) double-counts debt already inside assets, leaving what is effectively a trivial profitability-minus-leverage composite with a muddled economic interpretation.

This is largely a recombination of two archived signals ("Profit Peak Equity Sale" and "Cash Profit Payout Switch") — swapping MIN for a signed payout-vs-issuance spread on the same TS_RANK profitability conditioner — and the archived peak-issuance version already showed a *positive* significant long-short alpha directly contradicting the negative expected sign, which the proposal does not diagnose.

This is a single-operator substitution (level dlc/lt → DELTA of dlc/lt) inside the already-tested "Profitable Cash Maturity Spread," i.e., a cosmetic variant, and the archive repeatedly shows one-year debt-ratio changes contribute little signal on their own.

Converting both legs of the successful "Low Cost Liability Profit Quality" from levels to five-year trends is a substantive shift from quality-level to improvement content and the MIN construction is internally consistent with the positive sign, though the interest-burden trend leg risks loading on rate-cycle/refinancing timing and five-year trends will cut coverage.

Internally consistent and economically interpretable (high-growth self-funded margin expanders versus issuance-funded growth), but the external-financing leg is close to the well-known net-external-financing/composite-issuance anomaly, so incremental content will hinge on the sales-growth × margin-change interaction.

A defensible hybrid that replaces the issuance screen of the archived R&D cash engine with current-debt maturity pressure, and the expression matches the hypothesis, though COALESCE(xrd,0) plus the RANK multiplier concentrates the entire spread in R&D-heavy firms, raising breadth and stability concerns.

Both legs push in the same direction as the stated negative sign and the construction is coherent, but the horizon mismatch (five-year interest-burden trend versus one-year cash-flow change) is arbitrary and the signal risks being a repackaged distress/financial-constraint screen.

This is a one-leg substitution (dlc/lt → xint/lt) inside the archive's best-performing signal, and both the pre-R&D cash leg and the xint/lt cost leg have already been separately validated in the archive, so the incremental information is largely predictable rather than a genuinely new mechanism test.

Replacing the cash-level leg with cash-flow volatility is a defensible mechanism-discriminating test (level vs. durability) rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the archive's earlier volatility leg was weak and the 5-period VOL will thin coverage among young R&D firms.

Swapping the cash-profitability level for the change in operating profitability meaningfully re-specifies the issuer-quality leg and the expression matches the stated sign, but it overlaps substantially with the archived cash-backed-issuer signal since the accrual leg already embeds oancf.

This is the most genuinely new construct of the set — conditioning the debt-issuance channel on margin improvement and average liability cost — and it is internally consistent, with the only caveat that xint/lt is partly endogenous to recent issuance (new low-rate debt lowers average cost).

Coherent and correctly signed, but it mostly recombines legs already tested in the archive (sales growth gate, cash profitability, dlc/lt maturity pressure), and because RANK(GROWTH(sale)) is strictly positive the "growth gate" only rescales the spread rather than creating true conditionality.

The payout gate and the coverage leg are mechanically negatively related (payout is subtracted inside the coverage term), which muddies interpretation of what the interaction isolates, and the construct closely resembles the archived cash-covered dividend spread that already failed to deliver alpha.

This is essentially the arithmetic product of two already-tested archive signals ("Intangible Cash Maturity Shield" and "Growth Cash Maturity Match") with only a denominator swap (sale for at), making it a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism, and the triple-rank multiplication will concentrate the long leg in a thin R&D-heavy, high-growth cell that risks unstable portfolio composition at ~9% coverage.

The MIN(dltis, dltr) overlap as an identifier of genuine refinancing episodes is a genuinely new construction not present in the archive, and pairing it with a *change* in interest burden (rather than the level used in "Productive Debt Issuer Margin") is a substantive, economically coherent refinement, though it reuses the familiar scale-times-signed-spread template and inherits that predecessor's weak Fama-MacBeth evidence risk.

The second factor is character-for-character identical to the archive's "Productive Debt Issuer Margin" spread, with only the scaling variable changed from dltis to prstkc, and it also overlaps heavily with "Durable Cash Payout Cost Shield" — this is a variable substitution, not a new hypothesis.

The two spread components are largely redundant by construction — RANK((oiadp−oancf)/at) and RANK(−oancf/at) both load on low operating cash flow — so the signal collapses to a low-cash-flow indicator gated on dlc/lt, which is precisely the channel already tested by "Reported Profit Short Debt Stress" and "EBITDA Current Debt Wall".

A two-term difference of a profitability ratio and an average-interest-rate ratio is too trivial to constitute a cross-theme signal, and it re-treads the archive's "Low Cost Liability Profit Quality" channel (oibdp profitability minus xint/lt) with a monotone reformulation from MIN to SUB, while oibdp/lt is itself close to a mechanical profitability-times-inverse-leverage composite of two known anomalies.

Because oibdp/sale ≈ 1 − cogs/sale − xsga/sale, the spread RANK(Δxsga/sale) − RANK(Δoibdp/sale) is mechanically near-double-counting margin deterioration rather than isolating overhead-specific inefficiency, so the signal reduces to external-financing × margin-decline — the same channel as "Failed Lagged Capital Raise" (fmb −0.43) and the inverse of "Self Funded Sales Margin Growth"; the introduction of xsga is the only genuinely new element and it does not survive the accounting identity.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Current Debt R&D Retrenchment" (identical multiplier, identical cash leg, only DELTA(xrd/sale) swapped for NEG(TS_RANK(xrd/sale,5))), so it re-tests the same channel rather than a substantively different mechanism.

It reuses the exact issuance multiplier and oancf/at leg of the archived "Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality" and merely substitutes the well-worn dlc/lt maturity leg for the accrual leg, making it an incremental recombination of two already-tested components rather than a new hypothesis.

Internally consistent and a genuine reframing of the failed lagged-capital-raise idea into a profit-productivity-vs-asset-growth payoff test, though the spread leg is close to the well-known asset-growth and profitability-change anomalies and the non-negative issuance multiplier means magnitude of issuance will dominate the cross-sectional dispersion.

The construction is coherent with its stated economics (signed net retirement scaled by a [0,1] gate that is high only when both cash generation and interest burden are high) and it directly diagnoses why the earlier net-debt-retirement signal had a strong slope but no alpha; the main risk is that the high-xint/lt gate loads on distress and the gate compresses rather than reorders the signed paydown.

This is the archived "Profitable Cash Maturity Spread" with oancf/at replaced by NEG(DELTA(cogs/sale)) — same industry-profitability multiplier, same dlc/lt leg — so it is a cosmetic variant that also inherits the sign-flip of an already-tested gross-margin-squeeze idea.

Structurally this is the archived "Productive Debt Issuer Margin" with both legs differenced (margin change → cash-carry change, xint/lt level → xint/lt change), which is a delta-ization rather than a new mechanism, and it further overlaps "Levered Cash Carry Advantage" on the oancf/lt versus xint/lt comparison.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's best performer ("Intangible Cash Maturity Shield") with only RANK→IND_RANK on the R&D leg, so it re-tests an already-established result rather than a substantively new mechanism.

Internally consistent (the double-negative on oancf correctly makes high cash flow raise the score) and economically coherent as a "use of proceeds" refinement of the equity-issuance anomaly, though it is largely a recombination of the archive's "Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality" and "Cash Profit Net Debt Retirer" legs.

This swaps one leg of the archived "Debt Rollover Profit Cost Reset" (interest-cost change → current-debt-share change) while keeping the same MIN(dltis,dltr) gate and profit leg, which is a marginal variant of an already weak result rather than a diagnosed improvement.

The expression matches the stated hypothesis and the negative sign is correct for a non-negative distress composite, and the interest-cost-shock channel is a defensible economic reinterpretation of the archived "Current Debt R&D Retrenchment," though it remains a one-leg substitution on a prior signal and the MIN gate will make the tails sparse.

The operating-leverage-versus-overhead conditioning on lagged external financing is a genuinely different discriminator from the archive's asset-growth and SG&A-only versions, but GROWTH(oibdp) is unstable for firms with small or negative operating profit and the earlier lagged-capital signal delivered t-stats without alpha, so portfolio-side payoff is uncertain.

A new and interpretable leg (depreciation burden as maintenance drag on debt-financed assets) not present in the archive, but note that oancf mechanically adds back dp so the two ranked legs partially offset, and dp/at is strongly capital-intensity driven, making this partly an unneutralized industry bet.

This is a cosmetic re-weighting of the archived "Growth Cash Maturity Match" (RANK→INDICATOR on the same growth gate with an identical cash-margin-minus-current-debt spread), and the indicator additionally destroys information by collapsing all non-growers to exactly zero, which lands them in the middle of the spread's [-1,1] range rather than excluding them.

The construction is coherent, but TS_SUM(xrd,5)/at is close to a 5x-scaled smoothing of xrd/at for the persistent R&D spenders that dominate the long leg, so its cross-sectional rank will be very highly correlated with the archived "Intangible Cash Maturity Shield" (fmb 5.25, ls_talpha 4.64) — this is a robustness check on the best existing signal, not a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a component swap within an already-explored family — identical to "Current Debt R&D Cost Shock" with the R&D-cut leg replaced by a margin-decline leg, and overlapping "Current Debt Gross Margin Squeeze" — so it adds little beyond confirming that current-debt concentration times deteriorating fundamentals is negative.

This is a mechanical crossover of two archived signals — the rollover scaler MIN(dltis,dltr)/at from "Rollover Cash Coverage Strain" bolted onto the exact MIN(NEG(ΔR&D intensity), Δxint/lt) conditioning block from "Current Debt R&D Cost Shock" — with no new economic content, and the WINSOR'd raw scaler times a bounded rank product will be driven mostly by a handful of large refinancers.

This is a direct rediscovery of the archived "Externally Funded SG&A Productivity Gap" with the spread negated and the expected sign flipped (and financing narrowed to dltis only), which is the same signal up to sign and already tested weakly (fmb -0.76, ls_talpha 0.72); the hypothesis also says growth "follows" issuance while the expression is contemporaneous with no LAG.

This is the sign-flipped archived "Dilutive Buyback Cash Gap" with sstk/at bolted on, and the bolt-on is badly constructed — ADD(GROWTH(csho,1), RATIO(sstk,at)) sums two unranked, differently scaled quantities before ranking, so whichever has larger raw dispersion (typically the csho growth tail) silently dominates the dilution leg.
